statement: An explicit spiral compactification gives an actual boundary-fixed based disk loop whose generated group is transitive and whose full interior centralizer is the specified closed discrete free proper cyclic group. Every forward orbit of that cyclic group has the full boundary circle as its limit set. A named interior centralizer map nevertheless has no continuous extension at any boundary point. An explicit interior conjugacy takes the cyclic action to a parabolic Fuchsian action and takes that same map to a boundary-fixed homeomorphism, proving that this actual interior conjugacy does not identify the two relative centralizer subgroups.
depends_on: The explicit spiral coordinate and inverse, uniform bounded-displacement estimate, periodic and compactly supported shear comparisons, original based-loop formulas, full local-centralizer calculation, exact two-sequence boundary limits, and the specified upper-half-plane conjugacy proved here
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), admissible infinite-operator level-zero comparison and the actual relative disk extension problem.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The original disk topology, operator and loop labels, full interior centralizer, actual boundary limit sets, interior comparison map and its inverse, and both relative subgroups are explicitly retained.
computational_checks: code/part_b/c72_spiral_comparison_certificate.py and its adjacent JSON/stdout pass 38,263 exact symbolic and rational checks of the radial inverse, two asymptotic phases, actual parabolic conjugacy, centralizer map, and shear and loop formulas.
notes: The original loop has an explicit contraction obtained by scaling its four path amplitudes. The claim refutes only the displayed extension comparison, including the proposed use of transitivity and a full-circle orbit limit set. It gives no nonzero fundamental-group class, no infinite-operator level-zero counterexample, and no conclusion settling C.12. The same specified paths extend by identity across the complement of an embedded closed disk in a surface.
